title: Why Does Coffee Wake You Up? ☕
description:
Why does coffee wake you up? Caffeine doesn't give you energy: it blocks adenosine, the sleepy molecule your brain builds up all day, until the crash hits.

topic: Why does coffee wake you up? (caffeine blocks adenosine)
script:
Coffee doesn't give you energy.
It hides how tired you already are.
Your brain makes a molecule called adenosine.
The longer you're awake,
the more it piles up,
and when it locks onto your brain cells,
you feel sleepy.
Caffeine is shaped almost exactly like adenosine.
So it jumps into those docks first,
and just sits there,
blocking the sleepy signal.
But the adenosine doesn't leave.
It keeps piling up outside.
Five hours later, half the caffeine's gone,
and all that tiredness hits at once.
That's the crash.
The weirdest part?
Plants didn't make caffeine for us.
It's probably bug poison.
So, what time is your last coffee?
key_facts: Adenosine builds up in the brain the longer you are awake and binds receptors that make you feel sleepy
Caffeine is shaped like adenosine and blocks its receptors without activating them
Caffeine's half-life is about 5 hours on average
Scientists think plants make caffeine as a natural pesticide (Nathanson, Science 1984)
